subject: Hosted API: Proposal for commit uplift and tier reconfiguration
messages:
From: Alex Chan <alex.chan@retailflux.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API capacity — converting burst to committed for Q1

Sergio,

Quick note from our side — we expect sustained traffic for product search and chat during the retail peak in Q1. We're currently relying on burst buckets but would like to convert a portion to a committed monthly commit to reduce unit cost and lock in capacity.

Two asks:
- High-level economics for converting 200M tokens/month of burst to committed (what discount vs current hosted rates?).
- Any constraints on soft-throttle windows or rate tiers we should watch for (we have short spikes at hour granularity).

I'll loop in procurement if this looks sensible. We have a tentative budget but need timelines and an SOW to push the PO.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Chan
Head of Platform
RetailFlux
Mobile: +1 415-555-0198

[Attachment: rollout_snapshot_q1_usage.csv (CSV, 18KB)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chan <alex.chan@retailflux.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity — converting burst to committed for Q1

Alex — thanks for the context and the usage snapshot. See below for a concise path forward; attaching a short playbook that summarizes conversion options and operational steps.

Summary proposal (high level):
- Convert 200M tokens/month burst => 200M monthly committed (12-month term)
- Effective unit price: ~18% discount vs current on-demand hosted rate (includes reserved capacity pricing band + soft-burst buffer)
- Keep monthly burst pocket of 50M for unexpected spikes; auto-fallback policy enabled to avoid throttling while preserving committed economics

Operational notes:
- Billing: first month proration applied on the day the contract is executed; invoices will align to Redwood monthly billing cycle.
- Deployment: no infra changes required for you — we map committed capacity to your tenant and preserve routing; ops handoff to Jordan for any QPS adjustments.
- SLA & fallbacks: we'll maintain regional routing and a fallback to compatible model variant if capacity is constrained; this will be called out in the SOW.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Kimberly to confirm pricing tables and invoicing cadence.
2) RetailFlux to confirm procurement contact and PO timing.
3) I’ll prepare SOW + MAP link and a one-page summary for your legal.

I've attached: commit_uplift_playbook.pdf (playbook and timeline).

Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 646-555-0139

[Attachment: commit_uplift_playbook.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chan <alex.chan@retailflux.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity — converting burst to committed for Q1

Alex / Sergio — following up with the numbers Sergio referenced. I attached a spreadsheet with the math and two pricing constructs: 12-month term (recommended) and 6-month term (shorter commitment, slightly lower discount). Key points:

- 12-month commit (200M tokens/month): 18% discount vs on-demand; effective monthly invoice will be billed in arrears with proration applied for month of transition.
- 6-month commit: 12% discount, option to expand earlier but higher unit cost.
- Soft-burst buffer: keep 50M token burst pocket; overage beyond committed + burst will be billed at on-demand rate with overage notifications and two-stage throttling (gentle rate-capping then hard throttle).

Billing mechanics we recommend:
- Execute SOW and PO before Dec 10 to ensure January billing aligns with committed capacity. If PO arrives after Dec 10, first committed invoice will be pro-rated for the remainder of the month and full from Feb.
- For accounting purposes, we'll provide a pro-forma invoice on signature to speed PO approvals.

Action items for procurement:
- Procurement: please confirm required PO language and the billing contact we should send invoices to.

Kimberly Park
Senior Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

[Attachment: pricing-model-v2.xlsx (XLSX, 56KB)]

Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity — converting burst to committed for Q1

Thanks — that looks reasonable. Retail leadership has approved the 12-month path for the 200M/month commit. Procurement: Jordan Ward (cc'd) will coordinate the PO and standard T&Cs.

Two quick asks from our end:
- Can you generate an SOW and a pro-forma invoice we can attach to the PO?
- We need the MAP link and a short rollout timeline so our engineering and finance teams have dates.

If we can get SOW + pro-forma by Monday (Nov 23), procurement will try to cut the PO the same week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex
